Short description, link fixes, image size, portal, cleanup, etc
Adding contrast to Madison use of the word 'democracy', it wasn't always as 'direct democracy' as seen in the federalist papers
Madison doesn't consider that democracies "become weaker", the larger they are, he takes for granted they have a maximum size.

Founding fathers criticized direct democracy, but the idea that it was "due to the lack of a constitution enshrining inalienable rights" makes no sense, written constitutions didn't exist, for any form of government before american revolution. Founder themselves use 'constitution' meaning 'unwritten constitution' many times, founders believed the ancient democracies had constitutions but direct democracy itself was seen as a problem not the lack of specific laws
The concept of democratic republic passes to the general section of democracy

The affirmation 'The overthrow of the roman kingdom created the first state with the purpose of being a republic' makes no sense, as this same page explains, romans didn't use republic as a name of a specific form of government but 'political society' in general. And there is no reason to think roman republic is previous to greek ones
